citation_with_page: Snow (1855) On the Mode of Communication of Cholera 2nd ed. via Project Gutenberg #72894 https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/72894 (page numbers not in the transcription; section given); Snow section on Thomas Street Horsleydown: Surrey Buildings (11 deaths from a well fouled by a gutter) against Trusscott Court (1 death) on the same Southwark and Vauxhall mains; Mr Grant report to the Commissioners of Sewers; death dates run to 10 Aug 1849

Snow (1855) On the Mode of Communication of Cholera 2nd ed. via Project Gutenberg #72894 https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/72894 (page numbers not in the transcription; section given); Snow section on Albion Terrace: houses sharing a contaminated spring supply had about 20 deaths while neighbouring houses stayed free; last death 13 Aug 1849

Snow (1855) On the Mode of Communication of Cholera 2nd ed. via Project Gutenberg #72894 https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/72894 (page numbers not in the transcription; section given); Snow reporting Dr Lloyd to the South London Medical Society 30 Aug 1849: 80 cases and 38 deaths in a fortnight in early July 1849 on one fouled well (date an upper bound)

Snow (1855) On the Mode of Communication of Cholera 2nd ed. via Project Gutenberg #72894 https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/72894 (page numbers not in the transcription; section given); Snow reporting Dr Lloyd 30 Aug 1849: 25 cases and 14 deaths in houses drinking a ditch fouled by their privies against 1 case in the house with a railed-off pump (date an upper bound)

Snow (1855) On the Mode of Communication of Cholera 2nd ed. via Project Gutenberg #72894 https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/72894 (page numbers not in the transcription; section given); General Board of Health Report on the Cholera of 1848 and 1849 p. 62 as quoted by Snow: 30 houses on one fouled pump-well had 26 cholera cases and 25 deaths while 60 neighbouring houses on other water had no cholera case (date an upper bound; GBH report primary not seen)

Snow (1855) On the Mode of Communication of Cholera 2nd ed. via Project Gutenberg #72894 https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/72894 (page numbers not in the transcription; section given); Snow citing Dr Thomas King Chambers: a row of houses at Ilford on a fouled well was visited in every house but the one that fetched other water (summer 1849; date an upper bound; personal communication)

Snow (1855) On the Mode of Communication of Cholera 2nd ed. via Project Gutenberg #72894 https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/72894 (page numbers not in the transcription; section given); Snow: houses at Locksbrook near Bath with cesspool drainage in the well had a very fatal outbreak in autumn 1849 (date an upper bound; account passed on to Snow)
